_comment: Baselines for bench/value-ref-resolution/measure.mjs --check (#3399). Counts and `fingerprint` are CORRECTNESS gates over a synthetic Zig corpus whose shape is fixed in measure.mjs: `resolved` is every value-ref site resolveValueRefTarget binds, `declined` the two per-module controls it must refuse (a non-callable namespace member `dom_utils.DEFAULT_NS`, and the non-callable bare argument `Bridge(ElementN)`), and `fingerprint` an order-independent sha256 over every (site -> resolved target) pair. Drift in any of them means the resolved target set moved — a behaviour change to explain, never a number to re-baseline for green CI. Per module: 12 CONTAINER registrations (`ElementN.getJ`), 1 NAMESPACE (`dom_utils.compare`), 1 HUB (`hub.compare`), 1 BARE (`register(onTick)`), and the 2 declines — 17 sites, 15 resolved.
_linear_scaling_note: (t_large/t_small)/(320/80). ~1.0 is linear; measured 1.00-1.09 across runs on an M-series laptop, with `us_per_site` flat at 1.4-1.5 between the arms — per-site cost independent of workspace size is the property this gates. The four resolution channels each consult a wider index than the last, and channel 4 (CONTAINER) reaches `scopes.qualifiedNames`, a workspace-wide index: keyed it is O(1), scanned it is O(files) per site and this factor goes to ~4. Verified load-bearing by making that lookup a scan, which took the factor to 3.7.
_ms_budget_note: Timing budgets are deliberately loose (~50x the measured 2ms / 8ms) and exist only to catch an order-of-magnitude regression on a shared CI runner. `linear_scaling_slack` is the gate with teeth.
